chapter: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
title: Debut Records and keeping control of his publishing
summary: Mingus ran his own label and publishing because he saw what happened to others.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Oh, okay. Well, when you do, I'd like to hear it. Well, Debut was your own record company, wasn't it?

You know, You were unique in one regard, in that you took care of your own music. In other words, you had a Jazz Workshop and you published your own songs, you didn't let anyone else get a -- you didn't sell them outright to anybody, or assign the publishing to somebody else. And you had your own record company, and you kept control of your own music in a way that virtually nobody else at that time did.
Yeah, because I could see what they were doing to other people.
That still took some guts to buck the system. I mean, it wasn't easy to do it.
I imagine if you -- it if was like it is today, where people insist on having their publishing rights to your pieces in order to put a record out, -- but it couldn't have been easy.
